(a) The purpose of this chapter is to regulate alcoholic liquors and establishments dealing
               in alcoholic liquors for the public health, safety, and welfare of the township and
               persons within its jurisdictional boundaries. (b) This chapter is designed to establish reasonable and uniform regulations to prevent
               potential adverse impacts relating to alcoholic liquor. The regulations of this chapter,
               including those provisions relating to the issuance, transfer, renewal, or revocation
               of liquor licenses and permits, are designed to provide objective and orderly procedures
               for the administration of this chapter. (c) The township board finds that nudity, partial nudity, and sexualized conduct in alcoholic
               liquor establishments begets undesirable behavior, including violations of the law
               and dangers to health, safety, and welfare of the public, and based on evidence of
               adverse secondary effects associated with certain conduct in alcoholic beverage establishments,
               which effects have been presented in hearings and reports made available to the township
               board, and on findings, interpretations, and narrowing constructions incorporated
               in numerous cases…

questions.prompt: What is this chapter of Westland city code officially called?
questions.answer: The Liquor Control Ordinance
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 36-B, adopted Aug. 16, 2010, amended ch. 10 in its entirety to read as herein
               set out. Former ch. 10 consisted of §§ 10-1—10-3, pertained to the same subject matter
               and derived from the 1981 Code; and Ord. No. 36-A, adopted Feb. 17, 1998. Charter reference— Police power of city, § 3.2(b)17. Cross reference— Businesses, ch. 26; emergency preparedness, ch. 38; parks and recreation, ch. 66. State Law reference— Michigan Liquor Control Act, MCL 436.1 et seq.

This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the "Liquor Control Ordinance." (Ord. No. 36-B, § 1, 8-16-10)

The purpose of this chapter is to allow the city to establish and administer a policy
               for the issuance and transfer of liquor licenses, to provide for the enforcement of
               liquor laws, regulations and ordinances, and to manage the number of liquor licenses
               in the City of Westland. As used for the purpose of this chapter, the word "liquor"
               shall mean "alcohol" and/or "alcoholic liquor" as defined in MCL 436.1105. (Ord. No. 36-B, § 2, 8-16-10)

New liquor licenses or permits, transfer of ownership of existing licenses, transfers
               into the city of new licenses, and relocation or expansion of an existing licensed
               establishment will be approved at the sole discretion of the city council. (Ord. No. 36-B, § 3, 8-16-10)

(a) Business operation. All on-premises licensees shall operate in accordance with a plan of operation approved
               by the city council. (b) Plan of operation. A plan of operation shall contain an operational statement outlining the proposed
               manner in which the establishment will be operated, including, but not limited to,
               the format, schedule of the hours of operation, crowd control, security, alcohol management,
               use of the facilities, parking provisions, plan for interior use…

questions.prompt: Who enforces Michigan’s construction code in White Pigeon Township?
questions.answer: Township building officials
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Cross reference— Environment, ch. 10; land divisions and subdivisions, ch. 14; utilities, ch. 30; building sewers and connections, § 30-59; zoning, ch. 34; accessory buildings, § 34-402; unsafe buildings, § 34-410; building grades, § 34-411; moving of buildings, § 34-414; nonconforming uses, § 34-441 et seq.; site and building hazard and nuisance prevention, § 34-551 et seq.

Footnotes: --- ( 2 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 63, § 5, adopted March 1, 2011, amended Art. II in its entirety to read as
               set out herein. Former Art. II, §§ 6-31—6-33, pertained to similar subject matter
               and derived from the Code of 2005. State Law reference— Single state construction code, MCL 125.1501 et seq.

Pursuant to the provisions of the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction
               Code Act, Public Act No. 230 of 1972 (MCL 125.1501 et seq.) (hereinafter referred
               to within this article as the "Act"), and specifically section 8b of the Act (MCL
               125.1508b), the township building officials have been and will continue to be designated
               as the enforcing agency to discharge the responsibility of the township under the
               Act. The township has assumed responsibility for the administration and enforcement
               of the Act and the State Construction Code promulgated under section 4 of the Act
               (MCL 125.1504) and the township will continue to administer and enforce the Act and
               the State Construction Code throughout its corporate limits. (Ord. No. 63, § 5, 3-1-2011)

The township, through its building officials, shall also enforce the appendices to
               the codes that make up the State Construction Code, including Appendix G (Flood-Resistant
               Construction) of the Michigan Building Code. (Ord. No. 63, § 5, 3-1-2011; Ord. No. 64, § 1, 6-7-2011)

            for the safety of persons and property, do hereby ordain and establish this charter
            for the City of Williamston. Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Printed in this part is the Charter of the City of Williamston, Michigan, as adopted
               by the voters on January 3, 1961. Amendments are indicated by parenthetical history
               notes following amended provisions. The absence of a history note indicates that the
               provision remains unchanged from the original. Obvious misspellings have been corrected
               without notation. For stylistic purposes, a uniform system of headings, catchlines
               and citations to state statutes has been used. Additions for clarity are indicated
               by brackets.

____________ CHARTER TOWNSHIP OF WINDSOR STATE OF MICHIGAN ____________ Published in 1996 by Order of the Township Board ____________ PREFACE This is a compilation of the zoning ordinances of the Charter Township of Windsor,
            which includes the currently operative Zoning Ordinance of _______ _____, 19___, compiled
            with all amending ordinances through and including Ordinance No. 25, adopted September
            22, 1996. The chronological listing of all zoning amendments includes their location
            within the compilation and provides a valuable record of changes to the original Zoning
            Ordinance. Section headings in boldface type have been provided, if not supplied in the original
            copy, to facilitate usage. Sections that are subsequently amended are followed by
            a history note indicating the adoption date of the amendment. Cross reference notations
            are included to provide quick referral to other ordinances and/or sections dealing
            with similar subjects; any references not preceded by the Zoning Ordinance part number
            110 will be found in the separate volume of compiled general ordinances. Running heads at the top of the page contain an abbreviated article title and section
            numbers to provide a guide for locating specific information quickly. The section

questions.prompt: What counts as Zilwaukee’s park and swimming pool complex?
choices: The area inside the four-foot fence around the park
All city-owned land along the Saginaw River
The swimming pool and the boat launch together
questions.answer: The area inside the four-foot fence around the park
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Authority to operate recreation and playgrounds, MCL 123.51 et seq.; playground equipment
               safety act, MCL 408.681 et seq.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Park and swimming pool complex means the area embraced by the four foot fence surrounding the park boundaries. (Ord. No. 32, art. I, 7-6-1982)

(a) Rules and regulations adopted by the city council, and signs posted in the park and
               swimming pool complex shall be obeyed at all times. Violation of any posted rule,
               regulation or sign shall be grounds for expulsion from the park and swimming pool
               complex. (b) The city council shall set fee's by resolution for the use of the park and swimming
               pool complex, or any part thereof, from time to time. (Ord. No. 32, art. II, 7-6-1982)

(a) Persons violating a posted rule, regulation or sign shall immediately leave the park
               and swimming pool complex after having been orally told to do so by a city employee
               and be responsible for a municipal civil infraction. (b) Failure of a person to immediately leave the park and swimming pool complex when orally
               told to do so as aforesaid, shall constitute a misdemeanor. (Ord. No. 32, art. III, 7-6-1982)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates

               Johnson Street, if Johnson Street were extended to the Saginaw River. Riverfront Park means the area of the west shore of the Saginaw River leased by the city…
